abstract: Organoids are complex, miniaturized three-dimensional structures that replicate key biological features and functions of human tissues and organs. These characteristics make them powerful model systems for investigating tissue and organ development, homeostasis and regeneration; understanding disease mechanisms; and advancing drug development and personalized medicine. To fully harness their potential, it is essential to develop advanced tools capable of comprehensively profiling their intricate composition. In particular, cutting-edge technologies are needed to accurately characterize their genotypic and phenotypic profiles, including DNA, RNA, proteins and physiological functions. In this Review, we examine molecular and functional profiling methods for organoids, providing an overview of emerging techniques, recent advancements, future technologies, key knowledge gaps and challenges, and a framework for multimodal integration of methods. Additionally, we examine current barriers to progress and explore opportunities to refine organoid profiling methods with the aim of deepening our understanding of organoid biology.
